## 503. A death's way to the nearest temple: A* inside an area, no walk where there is no way

perf found a player's death stalling the server 1.5 to 2.8 s ("hits" in
the tick's slow line, decision 469): Main._return_place asks
Holdings.nearest for the nearest temple or healer's hut, three times (all
kinds, then each), and each asks WorldRoutes.route for every such place.
A route inside one area walked _flood from the fallen's cell, which stops
only once it reaches its cell, so most of the wilds each time; before the
distance fields are in (the raids' routes are made on the first death),
every portal of every area was flooded to, and a portal it cannot reach
floods the whole area; on netbench, with no links, the routes to the
wilds' temple flooded the wilds though nothing could get there.

Now:
- WorldRoutes._steps_between: A* by buckets in half steps, aimed by the
  octile distance (never more than the walk, so it finds a shortest one;
  world_map_test checks it against the flood on every cell of a room and
  on the wilds). The walk inside one area uses it.
- A route to an area the from area cannot lead to returns none at once
  (_areas_from), nothing walked.
- Until an area's fields are in: a walk inside it is its own walk alone
  (not every portal's as well); its portals are joined pairwise by A*;
  the walks from the start and to the end to its portals are A* each.
- Holdings.ranked: the reachable places of the kinds nearest first
  (nearest is its first); Main._return_place takes the first that is
  manned, routed once. That is the doc's "nearest manned return place";
  before, a second temple manned behind an unmanned nearer one was missed.

Measured on levels/ (the wilds' healer's hut and temple), one nearest
call: from the middle of the wilds 653 ms with the fields in and 3785 ms
before them, to 24 ms either way; across the wilds 420 to 18 ms; from the
castle before the fields 719 ms to 411 (other areas' pairs still walked);
a death made three such calls and now one ranked. On netbench (no links)
the routes to the wilds walk nothing.

Rejected: building the raids' routes at boot so the fields are always in
(threads in every hosted test, and the fallback still has to be cheap);
caching each place's distance field (a field per temple per faction for a
lookup made at a death).

## 501, companions' side (npc's sickness; the seam agreed with npc)

A companion resting in town falls sick as the town's people do (npc's side
above); this is her player's side of it.
- Where it lives: her player's companion card, companion["sick"] {since,
  kind, treated, cured_by}, written by npc's Townsfolk through Main while
  she rests in town (442). When it ends there, Main's
  _end_companion_sickness leaves companion["was_sick"] {since, ended,

  with <player> all the same."; she is never kept from her player. A
  player in another zone is told she "is sick in her bed in <town>"

  well again.", or "it ran its course"), a fact on her (294), and a
  narration to her exchange, so her next line can speak to it; then

  out of town, so Main._sickness_in_party (the world tick) ends it:

  join. She never dies of it, and it costs her nothing in the field this
  step. A remedy in her hands in the party is not this step: her
  sickness is cured by the town, or runs its course.
companion_test _test_sickness. Protocol unchanged; no new class_name.

## 504. Trade routes: caravans between a town and a market, raidable where they pass a camp

Economy's phase 2 of the gold economy (Jeff: "trade with other town. think
about establishing trade routes, also introduce luxury goods that traders
seek, sell to the rich"; the roadmap: "traders carry goods along maps'
routes between towns, routes on the world map and raidable"). Maps owns the
route, the walking, the raid hook and the arrival; economy owns the goods,
the prices, who goes and the trip home.

- Ends: a town (its store's place id) or a market, `market:<key>` from a
  level's new "markets" key (Level.markets_from, WorldMap.markets(); a
  market off the floor is a WorldMap problem). levels/castle has one, "the
  castle market" at (16, 9) in the keep (the coordinator's placement, one
  entry to move). Today's route: wilds/store>market:castle; town to town
  needs nothing more once there is a second town.
- TradeRoutes (sim/trade_routes.gd, World.trade, server only): routes()
  each town to each market and each pair of towns that can be walked,
  {id "<from>><to>", legs, steps, areas, exposed}, over the world routes'
  open layer (Main: the raid groups' routes, one set of distance fields):
  the caravan is the town's, held ground no wall to it; a closed link
  (463) is no way, as for every route, so the forest's way on exposes
  nothing. Made when asked, again when a place changes hands and on
  use_map (465's regeneration).
- exposed: every sample_steps (4) along the way on ground nobody holds,
  the nearest camp in raid_reach (30) cells whose side is hostile to the
  town's. eta(route) is world ticks at steps_per_world_tick (10); risk(route)
  the chance of at least one strike, from each exposed sample's world-tick
  share of its camp's strike chance (strike_chance 0.15 at full worth, or
  enemy-ai's `strike` Callable). Economy prices from both. Rules from
  economy.json trade.routes, these by default.
- send(route, {items, goods, members}, from_end) -> caravan id (either
  end); position(id) {area, cell, fraction}, kept for visible traders
  later; walks on the world tick; saved in the snapshot ("trade"); signals
  caravan_left, caravan_arrived(at_end), caravan_raided(camp, taken),
  caravan_lost(why: "taken", "no way").
- A strike (each exposed sample passed this tick, each camp once) takes
  food goods (economy's is_food Callable; "food" and "meat" unset) and the
  people: each member through Towns.resident_taken, held at the camp
  (captive_held), rescuable as raid captives are. Nothing else: items and
  other goods stay (Jeff: raids take food and people only); no gold goes
  on a caravan (economy settles at the market). A caravan with neither
  takes nothing and walks on; one with nobody left is lost, its items
  placed at the camp (ItemBook), its goods in caravan_lost for economy.
- The world map: the "world" message's "trade", [{id, from_area, to_area,
  areas, caravans: [{area, fraction}]}] for the routes through areas the
  player knows (TradeRoutes.shown, WorldNews.trade), sent with the full
  message and again whole when it changes; WorldMapPanel draws a dashed
  brass way through the areas' boxes, a dot per caravan. No
  PROTOCOL_REVISION (release): an older client ignores the key, and a newer
  one with an older server draws no routes, today's map either way.

tests/trade_routes_test (new): the route, its exposed stretch, eta and
risk, gone with the camp; a caravan out and back; struck, its food and
both members taken and held at the camp, lost with nobody left and its
sword left there; struck with no food and nobody, nothing taken; no route
with the way gone; lost when its way closes under it; a restart; shown on
the world map and kept by the client. world_news_test's "trade";
level_test's castle market.

Rejected: visible caravans in awake zones now (economy: abstract for phase
2); gold on caravans; a route as a level link; raids taking items; a
passing event for tolls (later, its own step).

## 505. Streams with fords and bridges

Infrastructure for streams (the outdoors backlog; the coordinator's split:
maps the level data, the walking and routing, the editor and a generator;
terrain the drawing; art-kit the bridge's slots; environment's spate later).
Agreed with terrain on the data, with art-kit on the slots.

- Streams are ordinary water cells. level.json "streams": [{"path":
  [[x, y], ...]}], each stream's cells in order from source to mouth along
  its middle (Level.streams_from, terrain "streams"); terrain takes the
  flow from the order. A path cell that is no water, or not beside the one
  before, warns and the stream is left out; water with no entry is still.
- A ford is a legend kind, "ford" #6fa8e0: floor, its footing the ground
  round it (Level terrain "fords"). World.is_ford is new; World.is_water
  stays deep water (the throw splash and the walk checks read it so), false
  on a ford. World.step_ticks makes a step into a ford FORD_TICK_SCALE (2)
  times as long, the same on the server and in a client's prediction;
  WorldRoutes charges FORD_COST (2) a step into one (step_cost, in _flood's
  _relax, A* and distances_from), WorldMap areas carrying "fords". A ford
  beside no water warns ("in no stream").
- A bridge is a building entry {slot: "bridge", at, facing, length, width
  1 or 2} (Level.BRIDGE, in the new Level.SPANS_WATER: the well stands in
  water, a bridge spans it). Its rect is width across by length along its
  facing; all of it over water or fords, clear of other buildings, with a
  floor bank of one height beyond each end (Level._bridge), else left out
  and said. Laid into the terrain (Level._lay_bridges): its cells floor at
  the banks' height and footing, out of "water" and "fords" into "bridged"
  (the water still drawn under it), railing wall edges on its long sides
  ("railings"), which Fields.fences lets sight through, as a field's fence.

## 499. Players give toward the town's next build

Jeff (2026-10-18): "players bank goods for gold and if they want they
spend gold later to help the town with upgrades and defences - they buy
armor weapons and services to sink gold, players lose gold through
spend". Phase 1b of his gold economy, the coordinator's approval; npc's
player-facing "give" offer is "499, npc's side".
- Towns.shortfall(town): the town's first build job still queued (its
  materials not yet taken: a new building, a level, a repair; walls are
  its defences) and what the store lacks for it: {kind, job, steps,
  needs}. {} for none.
- Economy.contribution_wanted(town) -> {kind, gold}: the lacking
  materials at what the store pays for them (raw_price x store.buy), what
  the town owes its gatherers and haulers, and the builder's fee
  (Production.town_work_fee), less what was given already. A player can
  never give more than that, or than they have.
- Economy.contribute(town, player, amount) -> gold given: out of their
  gold for good (spending, the only way a player loses gold), into a fund
  for that build, not the treasury, so the treasury's floor doesn't hold
  it back. The fund pays, in order: deliveries of what the build lacks
  (Economy.deliver, before the treasury), what the town owes its workers
  when the treasury is at its floor (_pay_owed), and the builder's fee
  when it stands (Production.settle_fund -> Economy.settle_fund). The rest
  is the town's, into the treasury: on the build, or when the plan is
  dropped (no build job of it left, on Economy's tick). Never given back.
- Thanks: contribute.gold_per_xp (2) gold a point of town experience
  (contributed -> Main -> Towns.add_xp, "<player> gave N gold toward the
  inn"), so a giving town unlocks its next building sooner.
- The fund is saved (Economy "funds"). tools/town_soak --give=N has each
  test player give up to N a day, for the measure.
Protocol unchanged (npc's offer carries the amount). larder_test.

Measured with npc's soak (496), 30 days, 3 players, --give=5 against the
same run without it (apprentices and the leather fix on both sides). The
players gave 129 gold in the month, all toward the inn while it waited
on leather: it stood on day 25.0 against 28.2. The fund paid the
deliveries and what the town owed, so its workers borrowed less: loans
taken 14 and repaid 25, against 36 and 8 (the ledger's last 200 lines);
the hunter ended owing 4 against 17, the cook 3 against 24. But the gold
ends with the makers (the smith 151 against 88, the carpenter 119
against 75), and the treasury stays at its floor (4 on day 29 on both
sides): the officials went unpaid 254 times on both. Giving builds the
town; it doesn't pay its wages. What brings the makers' gold back to the
treasury is phase 3's luxury goods and their tax, sold to the rich.


## 506. The level editor's properties panel

level.json had grown keys only a text editor reached (links' targets,
starts, chests' contents, places, 504's markets, 505's streams and bridges,
465's regenerate block). The editor's select tool now selects any of them
and its panel shows and edits their fields (the coordinator's design).

- EditorFields (editor/editor_fields.gd, new class_name): one table, KINDS,
  per kind where it is found (config: the level's own keys; at: a list
  matched by "at"; keyed: an object by key; spawn: spawn_points; indexed: a
  list by index) and its fields, each {key ("a/b" inside an object),
  label, type, min, max, choices, required, of}. The types are a closed
  set: string, int, float, bool, enum, level, spawn, faction, item, items,
  region, rect, cell, cells (shown, not written), order and action. The
  panel (LevelEditor._fields_panel) builds a widget per field by its type
  and knows no kind by name: a new key is a row.
- Selecting: things_at(doc, cell), topmost first: a monster (its panel as
  before), a crate, cart or chest, a link, a start, a spawn point, a place,
  a market, a building, a stream, an anchor; a second click on the same
  cell selects the next. Esc (nothing selected) shows the level's fields.
- Writing: check() refuses a wrong type, a value out of range, an enum
  value not offered, a level there is not, a spawn point that level has
  not, a faction or item there is not, a rect off the map; the status says
  why and nothing changes. A value that may be is written by write() as
  one undo step: the whole level.json key it lives in replaced through
  MapDoc.apply_changes ("config <key>", which undo already knew). Then
  issues(): Level.parse of the doc and WorldMap's problems for this level
  (the game's own checks); those naming the selected thing show in its
  panel, red for what the game leaves out, and warn, not refuse (a link
  with no way back yet is a fair state mid-edit).
- Never offered: a key not in the table (no raw JSON), a cell thing's "at"
  (repaint it), deleting a required key. The one "at" a field edits is a
  market's (type cell), picked on the map, since nothing paints a market;
  the level's panel has "add a market", a click putting one down
  (add_market). An anchor's rect is picked by two corner clicks.
- A spawn point's name is renamed by rename_spawn: the links in other
  levels arriving at it (links_arriving, over the levels and the ones
  registered) are named in a confirmation first; agreed, each of those
  levels is opened as a MapDoc, its links changed and saved through it, so
  its level.json is written the editor's way.
- The editor draws each market (a diamond), each anchor (outlined) and the
  selected thing ringed (a stream's course, an anchor's rect).
- The every-key check: editor_test reads every config key sim/level.gd
  reads and fails on one that is neither in the table nor in
  EditorFields.NOT_OFFERED (legend, became, loot, clearings, roofs,
  town_walls, item_style, monsters, centre, herds, dead_ground: painted,
  laid by other tools, or not hand-edited).

tests: editor_test's panel: a link's level and spawn set, a spawn the level
has not and a level there is not refused, undone; a chest's item, a bogus
one refused; a place's holder, a bogus faction refused; the spawn point and
the anchor on one cell cycled; the spawn renamed, asking first, and the
other level's link saved arriving at the new name; a market put down,
named and moved; a stream reversed; the regenerate block's days set and 0
refused; an anchor's rect picked; saved, read back. The every-key check.
Its levels are in the test's scratch folder, never the shared overlay.

Rejected: a raw JSON field (bypasses every check); a per-kind panel script
(each new key a new script); moving painted things from the panel (the
paint is the truth for them); refusing on the loader's warnings (many are
fair mid-edit).

## 505, sound's side: a stream heard before it is seen, a ford waded

Terrain asked (the coordinator: the sounds are sound's; a stream heard before
it is seen, as the dark forest's rule has it). Two parts, client only.

- Running water is a new positional loop, amb.stream (3 Freesound takes,
  CC0: 231536, 415053, 446019), reach 16 cells. A stream is a line, not a
  bed: Ambience holds one loop per stream (Sfx.hold), at the point of its
  course nearest the listener (Ambience.nearest_on: the terrain's "streams"
  paths, middle cells in flow order, projected onto their segments, so the
  sound slides along the water as you walk). Each weigh (WEIGH_EVERY) steers
  it there (Sfx.steer: heard as any sound is, muffled by walls, not by the
  canopy; ducked with the beds). Held within reach + 2 cells, let go beyond
  it; the loops are rebuilt when the terrain's streams change (a new zone).
  The path is the stream's middle, its width (1 to 3) not recorded: a line
  source loses at most 1.5 cells (terrain).
- A ford (World.is_ford: floor, not water, since is_water is deep only) is
  stepped on as water: Client3D._step_sound's footstep kind "water"
  (sfx.footstep_water_small/medium/large by mass, as before for wading).

Tests: sound_kit_test (nearest_on beside a stream, round a bend, past its
end, one cell, none; the slot's reach); view_test (a stream two cells off
held across from the listener, let go out of reach). Both pass with the
external takes moved aside, where no loop is held.

Rejected: a few fixed emitters along each stream (gaps or doubling as you
walk; many players for a long stream); a bed weighed by distance to water
(no direction); terrain calling the cues (the coordinator: sound's).
## 476. The interface's panels redraw only when something changed

Ui, from the coordinator's list (Jeff: performance first). Measured on the
wilds town host (4 herds, a storm at night, the talk box and the pack shown,
1080p windowed) with a new tally, UiCost (render/ui_cost.gd, class_name
UiCost): each panel adds the microseconds its frame work took under a name,
and --test-ui-cost prints the average per frame at exit. Before: pack 0.295
ms/frame every frame, the HUD block (compass place, counter placement, the
cursor hint with its picks) 0.055, shop 0.006, talk 0.003; all 0.360
ms/frame. After (amended 2026-10-19, the off-peak run): pack 0.004 ms/frame (from 0.295), hud block 0.011 (from 0.055), shop 0.005, talk 0.002; all 0.023 ms/frame (from 0.360), over 16303 frames; the frame budget after, tools/frame_budget.ps1 on the same town (9 players, 4 herds, storm at night, minimap open, 1080p): median 2.26 ms, 99th 5.07 ms, worst 19.3 ms (no before was captured: the first run deadlocked the gate).

- PackPanel laid out both rows every frame (Items lookups, icon lookups,
  label overrides). It now keeps a signature of what it shows (the player,
  the open thing, shown, the icon source, copies of each shown entity's
  slots and slot_notes, a count of icons arrived through
  ItemIcons.icon_ready) and refreshes only when the signature differs;
  open(), the setters and _ready still refresh at once. The "landed" sound
  (a slot changing) is unchanged: every slot change is a refresh.
- Main picked the body under the cursor twice a frame (the target outline
  and the hint), cast the door ray, walked every entity and read the
  ground each frame. It now picks the entity once a frame and shares it,
  works the hint out again only when the cursor moved, the world ticked,
  the thing under the cursor or the typing state changed, sets the label's
  text (and resets its size) only when the words change, works the
  compass's place out when the player's cell or the tick changes, and
  places the counter panel only when the pack's rect, the shop's box or its
  own minimum size changed.
- The minimap looked like a redraw every frame in this tree's copy, but
  maps' 482 (ab96edb) had already keyed it to the marks' hash; nothing to
  do.

Behaviour unchanged (ui_test, items_test); client only; protocol unchanged.
## 507. Builder mode places every monster kind, from data

Builder mode's place tool offered only imp, brute and sneak, a list in its
own code, so wildlife and any kind added since could not be placed by
asking. Now the kinds come from data (BuilderSession.monster_kinds):
levels/monsters.json's (Monster.kinds), then the level's own
("monsters" in level.json). A new kind needs nothing in builder.

- place's enum (BuilderSession.tools) and the grid's characters
  (BuilderSession.chars) are built from them. The goblins keep i, b and s;
  any other kind takes its initial (lower case, then upper), else the
  first free of SPARE_CHARS.
- The prompt says each kind in a few words and how it idles when its
  entry doesn't say (its row's idle). The goblins are in lore's words
  (primer: the imp a Blood Rot goblin, the brute an orc, the sneak a
  kobold). Other kinds use their row's label, and for a wild animal its
  role (prey bolts, game charges when struck, a predator hunts its
  diet). A wild animal is placed in a herd on open ground, never in a
  camp.
- A kind with no colour in Level.LEGEND gets one in the level's
  level.json "legend" when it is first placed (BuilderSession.kind_colour:
  a hue from its name, none already used), so layout.png holds it.
  "legend" joins CONFIG_KEYS. MapDoc.set_config("legend") redraws the
  map's colours, so an accepted kind is saved as itself, not as void,
  and undo takes the colour back with it.
- The ghost draws a kind with no default colour as a monster.

Protocol unchanged. builder_test _test_monster_kinds.

## 508. Tall grass and cover

The outdoors backlog and the hunting row asked for cover: "trees that block
sight and slow you, tall grass that hides you". Trees already stop a line
of sight (a trunk is a void cell). This adds the data and the sim for tall
grass; enemy-ai's perception decides what a look makes of it (the
coordinator's design, agreed with enemy-ai).

- The kind: "tall_grass" in Level.LEGEND (#a8c850), a cell painted in
  layout.png. It is floor on grass ground (kinds says "grass", so a view
  that knows nothing of it draws grass) and is listed in terrain
  "tall_grass". Under any building's footprint it is left out, said.
- Cover: World.cover_at(cell) -> 0..1, TALL_GRASS_COVER 0.7 on standing
  tall grass, 0 elsewhere, trampled or off the map. A PackedFloat32Array
  over the bounds of the level's tall grass (Zone.cover, cover_rect), one
  index and, on grass, one dictionary lookup for trampled: Senses calls it
  per perceiver per candidate. Only a number: the rule (moving or still, by
  GridEntity.last_step_tick; never in reach; never on a lit body; smell
  ignores it) is Senses', so there are not two rules to drift apart. Grass
  does not thin a line of sight: has_line_of_sight is unchanged.
- Slowing: step_ticks takes TALL_GRASS_TICK_SCALE 1.25 into standing grass
  (a ford's 2.0 first). Routes take no cost for it (FORD_COST stays the
  only one): too small to reroute anyone.
- Trampling: try_move's step off standing grass by a body of TRAMPLE_MASS
  40 or more (a player, a goblin, a deer; not a rabbit) flattens it for
  TRAMPLE_DAYS 2 (World.trampled: level -> {cell: the step it stands
  again}); flat, it has no cover and does not slow. The world tick stands
  it again when its time comes (_regrow), in every level, loaded or not. A
  body pushed in does not trample; only its own step.
- Saved: the snapshot's "trampled", level -> [x, y, step, ...].
- The wire: World.grass_changed(level, flat, stood) on the server is sent
  to the players in that level ("grass" {level, flat, stood}, flat
  [x, y, ...] each); a player coming into a zone is sent its whole set
  ({level, full, flat}). A client keeps it in World.trampled (grass_told)
  and emits grass_changed for terrain to redraw the trodden path. The
  level's tall grass itself comes in its files, as fords do. A new message
  kind and a new cell kind: PROTOCOL_REVISION 20.
- Laying: TallGrass.lay(map, rect, seed, {meadow, edge, keep_clear}) (new
  class_name, sim/tall_grass.gd) returns AreaTools-style changes: grass
  cells over a noise threshold (meadow 0..1, 0.5) and, with a 0.8 chance,
  those within edge (2) cells of a tree; grass only; never on or beside a
  marker, a stair, a door or a kept cell. The editor has "tall_grass" in
  its palette and "tall grass" among its area fills (keeping clear of
  level.json's spawn points, places and markets), one undo step.
- levels/sample has a patch (x 5, 7, 8 by rows 1 to 4), a trodden line of
  plain grass down x 6. Nothing in the wilds or the forest until Jeff asks.

Left to others: enemy-ai wires Senses.sees and glimpses; terrain draws tall
grass as a scatter that bends, and the trampled set; sound a rustle on a
step into standing grass (a step variant by cover_at; nothing new in
Senses). Crouching is not in v1 (a player stance and an input, items' and
ui's if it is wanted).

tests: tall_grass_test (new): the kind, under a building left out, cover,
the step's slowing, trampling by mass, standing again on the world tick,
the snapshot's form through JSON, a client's full and changed messages,
TallGrass.lay (grass only, clear of a link and a kept cell, a band by the
trees, the same for the same seed), the sample's patch. editor_test: the

Rejected: a concealed() rule beside Senses' (two rules drift); thinning the

## 504, economy's side: a town's caravans sell its surplus at the market

Jeff (2026-10-18): "trade with other town. think about establishing trade
routes" and "everything has to be gathered and someone paid to do it".
Phase 2 of his gold economy, the coordinator's approval; maps' routes and
caravans are 504 itself (TradeRoutes).
- Once a day (Economy's tick, _trade_turn), for each route between a town
  and a market (Main sets economy.trade_routes from World.trade.routes(),
  with each road's eta and risk), a town with no caravan out may send one:
  a member of each trade in trade.caravan.goes, then a hauler, none off
  work, outside, a master or an apprentice. It loads what the market wants
  (markets.<id>.wants), most wanted first, up to caravan.load a member,
  only what stands above the larger of the town's comfort and caravan.keep,
  plus what the first queued build costs and what the town makes what that
  build lacks from (the hides for the inn's leather). It goes only if the
  sale would fetch more than the members' trip wages and risk x the goods'
  worth. Members are away until home.
- The market pays value x want x (1 + risk_premium x risk), less as it
  fills: / (1 + bought / saturation), bought falling by caravan.recover a
  day. Phase 2's market has no purse of its own: its gold is unbounded and
  is the known source of new gold in the economy; saturation is its brake.
- At the market each member is paid the trip wage (caravan.wage a day of
  the round trip, eta x WORLD_TICK_STEPS each way); buy_share of what's
  left buys the market's "sells" good the town is shortest of, at value x
  caravan.sell, carried home; the rest goes to the treasury whole and
  untaxed ("trade:<market>", the coordinator's ruling).
- Raids take goods and members only (Jeff: raids take food and people):
  no gold travels, and a lost caravan's members come home unless taken.
- Each going, sale, return, raid and loss prints an "[economy]" line.
- Economy.caravan_sold(id, town, market, proceeds, wages) after each sale,
  for npc's road news (whether the wagon sold well).
- Saved: Economy "caravans", "bought", "trade_day".
Soak (30 days, 3 players, against the apprentice soak): 21 caravans to
market:castle, mostly food and wood, fetched 112 gold, 21 in wages and 86
to the treasury, none raided on its road. Officials unpaid 236 against
254; the treasury still ends at its floor (2 against 4), the new gold
going out at once to what the town owed. The inn didn't stand in 30 days
(28.2 before): the tanner reaches his loan cap after day 21 and buys no
more hides, the leather the town owes him unpaid while the treasury is at
its floor, the shortfall phase 3's luxury tax is for. Protocol unchanged.
larder_test.

## 508, sound's side: a step into tall grass rustles

Maps' tall grass, the coordinator's routing: a rustle as a step's variant,
nothing new in Senses. sfx.grass_rustle (3 Freesound takes, CC0: 396013,
396014, 396016; range 4) plays over the footstep, as far as the step is
heard (Senses.step_radius), when Client3D._step_sound's creature steps into
standing tall grass (World.cover_at > 0). Trampled grass is quiet, except
for the step that flattened it: Client3D notes the cells World.grass_changed
reports flat (_flattened, kept FLATTENED_MS 1000), and rustles(tile,
flattened, now) counts them. A heavy body's step therefore rustles whether
the server's "grass" news arrives before its step or after it (on a host,

placeholder blip where the takes are absent); rustles() for trampled and

## 513. Rocks and cliffs

The last of the outdoors backlog: cliffs made of height, a way up them,
rocks, and sight over an edge (the coordinator's design, agreed with
terrain and enemy-ai).

- Cliffs are no new data. A height step between orthogonal neighbours
  already stops a step unless a stair joins a one-level rise
  (World.height_step), a body pushed off a ledge already falls
  (FALL_IMPACT_PER_LEVEL a level, kept: the coordinator), and Client3D
  already draws a rock face on any step with no ramp. A list of cliff
  edges would only drift from the heights (terrain).
- "slope" (#c8b878): a stair to the sim, its rise found as a stair's (the
  one orthogonal neighbour a level up; said as a slope when it has none
  or several), so World, routes and the views' ramps take it unchanged:
  it is in terrain "stairs", and in terrain "slopes" too, so terrain
  draws a ramp of its ground (kinds: the ground round it) rather than
  steps. A climb of two is two slopes in a row.
- "rock" (#6e6a64): no floor, and walled round as void is (Level's walks),
  so it stops a step, sight and routes as a wall does; listed in terrain
  "rocks" with its footing in kinds, so terrain draws art-kit's rock.small
  or rock.large over the ground rather than a tree (outdoors, void is a
  tree). Not a boulder (an entity that moves) and not void. Not in the
  canopy's trunks.
- Sight over a lip: World._line_of_sight, for sight (not has_clear_line's
  light and heat), takes ground higher than the viewer's own between the
  ends to stop the line, where before only ground higher than both ends
  did. From under a cliff its lip row is seen and nothing behind it; from
  on top everything below. One compare in the walk as before. The same for
  every caller (Senses, companions, the archer's clear shot: enemy-ai's
  ask); shot_line already stops at ground higher than the shooter. Every
  level with heights sees so now, the castle's included: intended.
- Outcrops.lay(map, rect, seed, {levels 1-2, slope_side, rocks, keep_clear})
  (new class_name, sim/outcrops.gd): an uneven blob in the area's ellipse
  (a ring as wide as the slope is long left round it) raised levels over
  the ground round it, a slope run out from the furthest raised cell of
  its middle row or column on one side (the given side, else by the seed,
  the others tried), the raised cells beside the run taken down so the
  ramp's sides stand at its foot (terrain's ask: no half face), and rocks
  on the lip (rocks 0.35 of it) clear of the slope's mouth. Only ground at
  the base height is raised; markers, stairs, doors and kept cells, and
  the cells beside them, stay down. Empty if no slope fits. AreaTools'
  changes plus "heights", one undo step through MapDoc.apply_changes.
- The editor: "slope" and "rock" in its palette (letters / and R), and
  "outcrop" among its area fills (keeping clear of level.json's spawn
  points, places and markets).
- levels/sample made 8 rows taller (grass, the stream going on down x 12
  to the map's edge) and an outcrop raised in the new ground (seed 5): two
  levels, a slope up its east side, three rocks on its lip.
- The wire: two new legend kinds in the level files: PROTOCOL_REVISION 21.

Left to terrain: the slope's ramp in its ground with cliff rock on steep
sides, rocks from art-kit's slots.

## 516. The level editor's copy and paste, and its climbs checked live

From the editor backlog (the coordinator): with 513's cliffs and slopes,
raising ground by hand matters, and a prefab was the heavy way to move a
few cells. Height painting itself was already there (decision 357: the
height tool, the area's raise, lower, level and hill, the stairs tool, the
heights view); this adds what it lacked, and a clipboard.

- Climbs checked live: LevelEditor.climb_problems() reads each stair and
  slope cell as Level.parse does (the orthogonal neighbours walkable, one
  level up, no wall or door between): none is "the stair (slope) at ...
  has no cell one level up beside it: it is floor", several "could climb".
  It is cheap (the stair and slope cells only), so the heights view tints
  those cells red each time it draws, and the height and stairs panels list
  them (eight, then a count) after every stroke, stair laid or area height
  change. Slopes draw their climb as stairs do (HeightTools.climbs takes a
  slope); rocks keep their letter.
- The stairs tool lays slopes as well as stairs (stairs_kind, its panel):
  HeightTools' stair and flight changes with their cells made "slope".
- Copy: Ctrl+C with an area dragged out puts Prefab.extract(map, config,
  area, Prefab.CLIPBOARD_KEEP) in LevelEditor.clipboard: what a prefab keeps
  (KEEP, unchanged, so saved prefabs are as they were) and the spawn points,
  starts, markets and streams a saved prefab leaves out. Only the streams
  wholly in the area go (a stream cut in two is no stream). In memory, for
  the editor session: not across sessions or levels, not the OS clipboard.
- Cut: Ctrl+X copies, then clears the area as one undo step: its cells to
  void, heights to 0, edges to clear, and level.json's keys of the copy set
  without what was in the area (LevelMap.moved_config dropping its cells),
  its entries and links going with their cells.
- Paste: Ctrl+V picks the stamp tool holding the clipboard (CLIPBOARD, at
  the top of its list); R turns it, a click lays it, one undo step through
  MapDoc.apply_changes, as many times as wanted, Esc letting go. After a
  stamp the panel's issues (Level.parse, WorldMap's problems) are read
  again. Prefab.stamp_changes merges what a copy brings: spawn points and
  markets as places already were (a taken name _2, _3...), starts added
  where the map has none on that cell, streams added.

## 450. The landing boots the exported server

What only the exported server pack hits turned up first on the box: a
resource the export filters leave out (art/audio, anything not listed for
a dedicated server), a script that loads only in the editor, a class the
binary-token scripts resolve differently. `tests/server_boot_test.sh` (and
its `.ps1`) is now a part of `tests/land.sh` and `land.ps1`, run beside the
suite, net_test and state_test under the landing's suite take of the gate:

- `--export-pack "Linux Server"`, the box's own preset, into a temp
  folder (about 10 s, 24 MB).
- The pack booted by this Godot's Windows release template (from the
  export_templates folder for its version), the same runtime as the box's
  Linux one. Release templates refuse `--main-pack`, so the template is
  copied beside the pack under its name (`server.exe`, `server.pck`, the
  console wrapper `server.console.exe`). It runs `--headless --server` on
  a fresh APPDATA with no snapshot, on ports of its own (17892 +
  the checkout's offset), and quits after 45 s.
- One headless client from the checkout joins once the server's
  "listening" line is in, so a zone wakes and ticks scripts from the pack.
  The test waits on log lines, not fixed times: beside the suite a client
  took over 6 s to join.
- It fails on a failed export or boot, a non-zero exit, no "listening" or
  "joined as" line, or any `SCRIPT ERROR` / `ERROR:` line in the export's
  or the server's log. A `push_error` put in `Main._ready` made it fail.

It runs about 60 s, beside the suite (about 150 s), so a landing takes no
longer. A Linux export can't run here, but
the pack is the same file the box loads; what differs (the OS) the box's
own boot after a deploy still covers. Tests only; protocol unchanged.

## 518. A level-placed captive: a camp's holds, taken as a raid takes

Builder's deferred ask: "a goblin camp holding a captive" placeable from
level.json, where today a captive exists only when a raid takes someone.
A place of kind camp may carry holds: [{town, resident, name, trade}]
(Level.places_from keeps it, validated; docs/levels.md). On the server,
after the towns are seeded and after a regeneration's rebind (465's path;
builder may call it after an accepted change), Main._place_captives takes
each hold of a camp a faction holds, once: the resident is a worker id of
the town, a resident's name, or role words "a <trade>'s <son|daughter|
brother|sister|father|mother|cousin>"; one not found is minted through
Towns.move_in with origin "placed" (economy's: past the room check as
"settled" is, since a placed captive leaves the roster the moment its camp
takes them; the trade given or the hauler's, the name given or drawn from
rescue.names), its kin the town's resident of that trade, first by id (any
resident when the town has none, said in the log), the pair written into
both cards as a founding does (ResidentCard.kin_facts, the "kin" ids). Then
Towns.resident_taken(town, id, "placed:<camp>", holder) and captive_held,
the path a raid uses, so the kin's rescue commission (331), the camp's
fall (camp_taken, free_held, note_rescue), the carried-home and
Townsfolk's "came home from" facts all run unchanged. The words invent no
raid and no date (Townsfolk.placed_captive): the captive's card "Tilda was
carried off by the Blood Rot; they hold her at their camp.", the kin's
"Tilda, his daughter, was carried off by the Blood Rot before you came;
...", the officials' "Tilda, Folk0's daughter, is held at the camp of the
Blood Rot, taken before you came."; the faction as lore names the camp's
holder, never a fixed word (ResidentCard.faction_name now reaches lore's
entry through factions.json's lore_id and falls back to its display name,
so "the Blood Rot" everywhere a card spoke of "the goblins" before).
Idempotent: the snapshot's "placed_captives"
(camp id -> the ids placed, in hold order) says what is placed; a world
saved before it has none and places each hold once on its first boot; a
minted id found already a worker is taken as placed. A camp gone from the
levels (a regeneration dropped it) frees its placed held home through
Towns.free_held, as a fallen camp does, and is forgotten; a fallen camp
(nobody's) places nothing until a faction holds it again, and then only
holds not placed before. Never in a real level: the sample has no camp
and no store, so only resident_test's road level holds one (a
carpenter's daughter of the test town). Server only; protocol unchanged;
no new class_name.

## 505, terrain's side: streams, fords and bridges drawn

The client half of maps' 505 (the coordinator's split; the design approved
as sent). Client only.

- The water mask (ground.gdshader and water.gdshader read it) grows from
  RG8 to RGBA8: r water, now a ford's and a bridge's water too, so a
  stream's shore runs on unbroken through its crossings; g the forest's
  ground as before; b a ford's shallows.
- Under a bridge the ground is the stream's bed, not the deck: its cells,
  floor to the sim at the banks' height, are water to the ground and the
  surface (Client3D._measure_streams: each bridged cell's bed the lowest
  level of the water and fords round its bridge, _bed_levels), their cliff
  faces as water's. A ford is floor under a shallow sheet: in the water's
  body, no scatter on it, its footing showing through.
- Client3D.flow_mask: an RG8 texture of the way each stream runs, a texel a
  cell, from the paths' order (each path cell the step from the one before
  to the one after; out across the width STREAM_REACH, 2, cells); still
  water none. water.gdshader carries its ripples and churn down it at
  FLOW_SPEED (0.6 m/s), two phases FLOW_CYCLE (1.6 s) long cross-faded so
  the drift never stretches; ponds as before. Over a ford it is pale and
  clear (0.4 of the alpha, no depth), with foam across its edges where the
  current meets it and flecks on it.
- A bridge: art-kit's bridge.wood.deck on each cell (its variant by the
  cell), .rail along the outer long edges, .end onto the bank past each end
  (art-kit's conventions: z along the facing; an end's +z onto the bank),
  at the deck's height BRIDGE_LIFT (0.04 m) up, so the water drawn under,
  WATER_LIFT up at a stream level with its banks, never shows through; a
  MultiMesh for each piece, variant and mesh. A bridge 2 wide takes an end
  a column (art-kit offers bridge.wood.end_wide if it reads wrong).
- Sound is sound's (8a4a61fc): the ford's footstep and amb.stream read the
  same terrain keys.

the flow down the path and none away from it, the bed under the bridge at

## 514. Luxury goods for the rich, and their tax

Jeff (2026-10-18): "introduce luxury goods that traders seek, sell to the
rich" and "taxes can be most higher on luxury goods which the rich prefer
then wages are paid by town". Phase 3 of his gold economy, the
coordinator's approval, amended once (the commission) after the first
soak; the catalog is "514, items' side" (wine, spice, silver_ring, tagged
"luxury").
- A luxury is a thing tagged "luxury" (Economy.is_luxury); its sale pays
  tax_class luxury (0.5) through the existing goods_class.
- The rich: residents whose purse stands above luxury.above (60). A folk
  need "luxury" each day (rich_every as often): with chance (purse -
  above) / luxury.span (100) they buy the cheapest luxury on the shelf
  they can pay from their purse (never on a loan), never one they made
  (the smith doesn't buy his own ring). Wine and spice are enjoyed (the
  book ends them); one tagged as luxury.kept (jewellery: the ring) is
  theirs, placed "resident:<id>" in the book. The card's trade both ways
  (note_trade: npc's facts and standing).
- A luxury asks at least its value (no want of the town's discounts it),
  an import at least its landed cost x luxury.markup (1.5)
  (Economy.item_price, for players' shop too).
- Imports: market:castle sells wine and spice. A going caravan, while the
  town has a rich resident and fewer than luxury.stock (3) luxuries on the
  shelf, orders one (the kind the shelf has fewest of, turn about by the
  day) at its landed cost, value x caravan.sell x (1 + luxury.carry x the
  round trip's days), dearer with distance. Paid for, in order: by the
  merchant (a resident of trade luxury.trade, on a loan under the bank's
  cap if he must), into the treasury now; else by a commission (amended,
  below); else by the treasury above its floor. The caravan buys it out of
  the sale (any shortfall from what was paid in on the going) and brings
  it home; it is not food, so a raid leaves it.
- On the shelf, an import is its orderer's (stock_shop maker), its landed
  cost kept (Economy "landed", saved): a sale taxes the merchant's margin
  over it at luxury 0.5 into the treasury, the rest his (Economy._sale's
  bought_for). A made luxury (the smith's ring, made by "always_want":
  "luxury", at most luxury.stock on the shelf, Production._serves) pays
  luxury 0.5 on its price as a made thing does.
- The commission (514 amended): the first soak moved nothing. The merchant
  had no gold and 20 owed against the cap of 30, the treasury sat at its
  floor, and the soak town has no ore for the ring, so no luxury was ever
  stocked while the smith and carpenter held 290 gold idle. Now a rich
  resident whose want finds nothing they can buy is the town's commission
  (Economy "commissions", one a town, saved). The next caravan with no
  merchant's order takes it: if they can pay the whole asking price, they
  pay the landed cost up front into the treasury as the order, and on the
  return the thing is theirs at once, paying the rest of the merchant's
  price (landed x markup, at least its value, by both their factors), the
  luxury tax on his margin to the treasury, the rest his. No new credit:
  the gold that moves is the rich's own. A buyer gone or short of the
  rest: it goes on the shelf, what they paid the town's.
- [economy] lines for each order, commission, purchase at the market,
  shelving, homecoming and sale, with the tax.
Soak (30 days, 3 players) against a fresh baseline on the same main:
12 commissions (Odo the smith 8, Pell the carpenter 3, Tam the farmer 1),
180 gold paid up front (to the castle market through the caravan's sale),
132 more on delivery: 48 luxury tax to the treasury, 84 to Snagfin, who
paid off his 20 owed. Odo's purse 158 -> 81, Pell's 131 -> 52. Officials
unpaid 204 (235); treasury end 5 (2); the tanner paid what the town owed
him 28 times (7), and the inn stood on day 23.4 (not in 30 days). No
ring was made: no ore reaches the soak town's smith, which waits for the
work-site step. Protocol unchanged. larder_test.

## 522. A build stalled on materials doesn't hold up the next

The coordinator's approval, after 500's soak (the pasture waited till day
23.5 behind an inn short of leather: one build at a time).
- A build job remembers when it was ordered (Production.order_build "at";
  one saved before this has none: long ago).
- Production.builds_stalled(town): every build the town has in hand is
  queued, its materials not in the store, ordered build_wait.days (2) ago
  or more, and there are fewer than build_wait.most (3). Then Towns.tick
  lets the town order its next build as if it had none (repairs, roofs,
  choose), and choose skips a kind already being built.
- The stalled one is kept at the head: the builder's bid takes the first
  queued build whose materials are in the store, else the first; 499's
  shortfall (what players give toward) is still the first queued build.
Soak (30 days, 3 players, against 500's): the pasture stood on day 8.1
(23.5), the shepherd came on 11.1 (26.5), the loom on 11.2 and the weaver
on 14.2 (29.6). The inn didn't stand in 30 days (23.4): the treasury,
at its floor, paid what the town owed the weaver (28 times) and the
shepherd (16) as well as the tanner, who was paid 8 times (25) and made 5
leather (13); the inn ended 2 leather short. Officials unpaid 198 (201),
treasury end 1 (5). Protocol unchanged. towns_test.


## 526. The sun's shadow map at 8192, blur 1.0

The sun (DirectionalLight3D, decisions 290-292) drew its shadows into the
default 4096 px directional atlas with shadow_blur 1.5, over
SHADOW_DISTANCE 70 m in one orthogonal split: a body's or a well's shadow
came out a mushy, speckled blob. Perf's sharpness bench (the coordinator,
from Jeff's "not crisp" note, 2026-10-19) found 8192 px and blur 1.0 turn
them into clean shapes: docs/shots/environment/sun_shadow_8k.jpg, today
left, 8192 right.

- Client3D sets RenderingServer.directional_shadow_atlas_set_size(
  SUN_SHADOW_SIZE 8192, 16-bit) as it builds the sun, and SUN_SHADOW_BLUR
  1.0; project.godot is untouched.
- Cost, measured (wilds town, clear noon, 9 players, 1920x1080, zoom 1.1,
  RTX 5090, 3 interleaved passes of 20 s): frame median 1.92 ms against
  today's 1.87 (today's own passes span 1.84-1.98), 99th 3.69 / 3.45 /
  3.89 against 4.61 / 3.52 / 3.84, GPU 0.4 ms either way.
- Memory: the atlas is 16-bit depth, 8192 squared is 128 MB of VRAM
  against 32 MB. There is no graphics preset yet; a smaller GPU pays the
  same 128 MB and a little more fill. If a low preset comes it sets
  SUN_SHADOW_SIZE back to 4096.
Client only, protocol unchanged.
Amended (2), the coordinator's (A): while the town's next build lacks a
raw (Towns.shortfall's needs), its maker makes it on the town's account,
498's store.town_account mechanism (the cook's meals) for that build only:
the materials from the store at no charge (Production._for_build, the
job's "account"), the raw the town's (deposited, not bought), and the
maker paid store.account_wage (3) for the job from the treasury above its
floor, owed if not (Economy.owe_or_pay, so it is among the head build's
debts paid first). Main and tools/town_balance wire Production.build_lacks
and town_pays. Soak (30 days, 3 players, against a baseline on the same
main): the inn stood on day 16.2 (not in 30 days), the tanner making 9
pieces of leather for it; the tanner's loan 20 at the end (25); officials
unpaid 200 (198), treasury end 5 (1). Still true, and not hidden by this:
a maker whose trade doesn't pay his keep (the tanner's margin on leather,
about 1.4 gold over two hides, against about 3 a day) is a finding for
the luxury step (514) and the apprentices (498 amended); this only stops

## 523. Fire drawn: flames, embers, smoke, and a flickering light

The castle's fixes asked for "fire that looks like fire (flicker, flames,
warm light), not flat yellow squares": a torch was a stone post with an
orange sphere, a fire cell a flat glowing patch, both under a steady light.
The coordinator's design, agreed with environment (the light) and art-kit
(the slots). Client only; the sim's fire (212) and light (123, 291, 304) are
untouched.

- Flames (new class_name, client3d/flames.gd) draws a flame: three crossed
  quads (flame.gdshader, rewritten) whose shape is a tongue torn by noise
  scrolling up, coloured on art-kit's row 7 from the bone core through
  ffd27a, ffb861 and e8792e to b8322a at the tips, unshaded, leaning
  downwind (309); a few embers rise out of it in the same shader and fade;
  over it one faint smoke quad turned to the camera (smoke.gdshader, at most
  0.15 of what is behind it), coming and going, gone by its top.
  Flames.light(parent, at, size, seed) puts one anywhere; Flames.at_socket
  lights a slot instance at its "flame" socket (art-kit's convention:
  prop.torch, prop.torch_post, prop.campfire, prop.forge), sized by the slot
  (Flames.SIZES: a hand for a torch, about a cell for a campfire), so
  whoever places a campfire or a forge gets its fire. None is placed in a
  level here.
- A torch marker stands on art-kit's prop.torch_post (a hazel pole in a
  ring of stones, its flame socket on its charred head) once the slot has
  art, else on the stone post as before; the flame on its top either way,
  the light over the flame. A fire cell keeps its ragged patch, with
  FIRE_FLAMES 2-3 flames of 0.45-0.75 m on it at places by the cell. Lanterns
  stay as they were: enclosed, steady.
- The light: only fire's drawn OmniLights flicker (Client3D._fire_lights,
  _flicker_fires), never World's light: Fields is the server's, and Senses
  thresholds it (237), so a flicker there would make bodies blink between
  seen and glimpsed. Flames.flicker: a slow sway (about 1.5 Hz) and a
  smaller flutter (about 7 Hz) on each light's own phase, a torch's
  TORCH_FLICKER 0.08 of its energy either way, an open fire's FIRE_FLICKER
  0.14; on the view's clock (accumulated frame time, so a fixed-fps capture
  flickers as play does); the energy only, never the light's place, so no
  shadow crawls. By day, outdoors only, the light fades toward DAY_SHARE 0.3
  by the look's daylight, less under the forest's canopy (477):
  Flames.day_share; indoors and in dungeons it burns full at noon.
- The warm pool on the ground: the floor's steady warmth near heat (304,
  _cell_shades, worked out when the fields change) is left as it is; the
  flicker reaches the pool through the light's energy alone (re-shading the
  cells each frame would cost a great deal: environment).

tests/view_test (the castle: a flame on each torch's top and two or three
on each fire cell, each with its smoke; flames sized by slot at its socket;
the flicker within its swing and the same for the same time; the day fade
outdoors only; each drawn light flickering while World's light stays).

Rejected: particles for embers and smoke (a node and a draw each per fire;
the shader's sparks cost nothing more); a prop.flame mesh slot (a flame is

marker is a free-standing cell; art-kit keeps the sconce for buildings'

## 525. Relief: hills, valleys and ridges as data

Jeff: "dirt having polys is not what i meant by elevation .. i meant hills
and valleys and ridges." Whole levels (356-358) and 513's cliffs read as
terraces. The joint design with terrain, approved by the coordinator:
terrain's polys fix first (524), this data half, then terrain's drawing
("525, terrain's side"). This is the first of maps' two landings under
this number: the data, the sim and the protocol. The generator
(Relief.lay), the editor's height brush and levels/hills remade follow.

- One elevation per cell centre, in metres (a cell is 1 m), so a cliff
  lies on the edge between two cells where 513's are and each side keeps
  its own corners. Outdoors a level may give it in relief.png: one pixel
  a cell, centimetres as R * 256 + G. Godot 4.7's PNG loader cuts 16 bits
  to 8 (checked: a 16-bit 256 read back as 1), so 16-bit grey would not
  do. Terrain carries "relief" (a PackedFloat32Array row by row),
  "relief_size" and "relief_given"; World holds it packed and swaps it
  with the zone, as cover.
- With no relief.png the field is derived from the whole levels at
  Relief.LEVEL_M 0.5 m, and every rule below gives today's answer on it
  exactly (indoors, the castle, the dungeon, every level made so far).
  Given both files, relief.png wins, said. height_at() and terrain
  "heights" stay, as the elevation rounded to levels, for buildings,
  bridges, light and the views until terrain's side reads metres.
- class_name Relief (sim/relief.gd), static so the sim, the routes, the
  views and the tools share one of each rule: cliff_between (more than
  WALK_RISE 0.45 m an orthogonal step, times sqrt 2 a diagonal),
  step (World.height_step's answer: a stair or slope climbs up to
  STAIR_RISE 0.5 m its own way; a diagonal needs both orthogonal routes),
  levels (a drop in whole levels, one at least), pace, corner_heights,
  flat, derived, whole_levels, read and image.
- WALK_RISE sits under a level's 0.5 m so a whole level's step stays a
  cliff. A stair is found as a cell 0.25 to 0.5 m up.
- Pace: a step rising r takes 1 + UPHILL_PACE 0.5 x r / WALK_RISE as long
  (World.step_ticks); a stair's 0.5 m is no slope and costs nothing more.
  WorldRoutes adds the same in half steps (climb_cost) to its floods and
  A*, and steps by Relief.step. World.find_path's own costs are unchanged.
- Falls: FALL_IMPACT_PER_LEVEL for each level of Relief.levels(drop).
- Sight, on a level with relief.png: a line from EYE_M 1.5 m over the
  viewer's ground to AIM_M 1 m over the seen cell's, stopped by ground
  above it (World._line_in_metres); shot_line likewise from the eye toward
  the aim. A wall is seen over by an eye more than WALK_RISE over both its
  cells (the old "higher than both", in metres). Light and heat keep the
  whole levels' rule. Without relief.png sight is as 513 left it.
- Pads: a building's and a roof's cells within PAD_FLAT 0.05 m of each
  other (Level._uneven), else left out, said as before; a bridge's banks
  likewise, its deck at the banks' elevation.
- Water: a water or ford cell holds its surface. A pond lies level within
  PAD_FLAT, a stream steps only down along its path, dry ground beside
  water stands SHORE_LIP 0.1 m over it (terrain's bank); said, not changed.
- The files: Level.parse, register, source and template take relief.png;
  WorldMap's digest and areas; BuilderHost's "terrain" message and its
  client side; MapDoc keeps and writes it (the editor's brush is the next
  landing). PROTOCOL_REVISION 22.
- levels/sample: relief.png in place of height.png, its whole levels
  lifted 0.2 m over its water, a gentle rise of 0.9 m east of the stream;
  its stairs, slopes and outcrop as before.
- Cost at 256 x 256: 64k cells, 256 KB of floats a zone; relief.png about
  100 KB on the wire, once a zone; a step check is array reads.

tests: relief_test (new): the rules, relief.png read, stairs by metres,

## 524. The ground's kinds meet softly: no "polys"

Jeff: "dirt having polys is not what i meant by elevation .. i meant hills
and valleys and ridges." Two things made the ground read as polygons: art-kit's
ground.dirt, whose flat polygon cells art-kit has remade soft (its own landing,
docs/art_picks.md), and the way ground.gdshader met one kind with the next,
which is this. The hills themselves are 525. Client only (ground.gdshader).

- The kinds texture (a texel a cell) was read bilinear, pushed by one fbm of
  up to 1.1 cells, then the strongest kind kept with a hard 0.18 band: the
  borders followed the bilinear tent's diamonds, so a dirt patch's outline
  was facets along the cell grid.
- Now it is read by Catmull-Rom (smooth_read: nine bilinear reads, smooth and
  through each texel's own value, so a lone cell of a kind, a one-cell path,
  still shows, where a B-spline would lose it), pushed at two scales: a slow
  drift of up to KIND_DRIFT 1.5 cells (an fbm about 3 m across) and a quicker
  wobble of KIND_WOBBLE 0.35 (about 0.7 m). The strongest kind is kept with a
  soft band (KIND_EDGE 0.25, a smoothstep, not a cut), so kinds meet along
  soft, frayed borders that follow no cell.
- Grass wears through the dirt in patches (GRASS_WEAR 0.7 of the dirt's
  weight given to grass where an fbm runs high), so a patch of dirt reads as
  worn ground, not a cut-out.
- Everything over the kinds (the season, wet, the forest's edge, light and
  heat, the floors) is unchanged.

Shots: the wilds town and the sample before and after, on art-kit's soft
dirt, beside the tone pairs (C:\dev\review\tone).

Rejected: a B-spline read (smoother, but a one-cell path of a kind vanishes);
a finer kinds texture (four texels a cell: the level's data is a cell's kind,
the warp gives the shape); dropping the strongest-kind band for a plain mix
(kinds would mud into each other).
Part two (the same number; protocol unchanged, f6a2296d1162): the
generator, the editor's brush and levels/hills.

  fbm roll (base, amplitude, scale), ridges and valleys along polylines

  (the rest falling away as a spur), keep_flat pads, then a slope limit of
  LAY_SLOPE 0.4 m a step (under WALK_RISE, so centimetres keep it walked)
  except across faces: an exact distance transform in raster passes (down
  to within the slope of the fixed cells, then up where the ground falls

  carved STREAM_DEPTH under its ground, never rising, its banks lifted to
  SHORE_LIP over it and kept while the ground round them is limited again.
  A laid area dipping under 0 m is lifted whole (relief.png holds nothing
  under). Returns {relief, cells (water), streams}. Relief.pad(map, rect)
  levels a footprint and a one-cell apron. Static, for the editor fill and
  the level tools (and builder's, if asked for).
- LevelMap.relief (PackedFloat32Array, empty for none), relief_field,
  relief_at, set_relief (to the centimetre), read_relief, to_relief_image;
  copy and transformed carry it (a grown side takes its neighbour's).
  MapDoc keeps it in its map (no longer an Image of its own), set_relief,
  apply_changes "relief" (cell -> metres), undo "relief x y"; a map's

- The editor: the height panel's "ground in metres"; on a map with relief

## 528. A living for the trades the town needs

The coordinator's livings audit (each trade's income and keep a day in a
30-day soak): the smith, carpenter, farmer and woodcutter clear their
keep; the tanner was paid less for leather than his hides cost, the
weaver's cloth covered only her wool, the shepherd and the haulers earn by
the load at value 1-2, and the officials were never paid (the treasury
always at its floor) while the smith and carpenter took about 34 gold a
day of mending and tools fees taxed at 0.1. Jeff's rules: "makers have
more expense", "everything has to be gathered and someone paid to do it",
"taxes can be most higher on luxury goods which the rich prefer then wages
are paid by town". Built on 498 (the store buys, makers pay for
materials); the coordinator approved A, B and C as one design, C flagged
to Jeff as the coordinator's to veto.
- A. A maker's price: the store pays a worker for a raw they made from
  raws (leather from hides, the bolt's cloth from wool: a catalog item
  made by their trade that yields it) no less than its inputs at the
  store's own sell price (as buy_materials asks them) plus
  store.make_margin (3) for the job, over the job's yield
  (Economy.maker_floor). raw_price's want discount works only above that
  floor; a gatherer's raw and a player's banking have none.
- B. A wage floor: once a day (Economy._floor_turn, "floor_day" saved)
  each resident of a trade in wage_floor.trades (shepherd, hauler, tanner,
  weaver, cook) whose work earned less than wage_floor.gold (3) a day since
  the last turn is paid the rest by the town, from the treasury above its
  floor or owed (as the head build's supplier first when the trade's good,
  wage_floor.trades' value, is what it lacks). Earned: Production.pay's
  gold less loans, founding gold, theft, fencing and the floor itself,
  and what the town comes to owe them when it is owed
  (Production.note_earned/take_earned, "earned" saved).
- C. The service tax by the earner's purse: a service fee (tools, mending:
  Economy._pay's "trade") earned while the payee's purse is above
  luxury.above (60) pays tax.trade_rich (0.3), below it tax.trade (0.1)
  as before, so the rich carry the town's wages and a struggling maker's
  fees aren't taxed harder.
- "[economy] <name> the <trade> earned N: the wage floor's M more, P paid
  and O owed" a top-up.
Soak (30 days, 3 players, against 522 amended (2)'s on the same main):
the weaver and the cook now clear their keep (loans at day 30: weaver 8
(28), cook 1 (24)); shepherd 16 (27), tanner 15 (20), hauler Bea 8 (25);
the inn on day 16.2 (16.2), treasury end 5 (5). The floor came to 258
gold over the run: 126 paid, 132 owed. Officials unpaid 229 (200): the
floor and the makers' price draw on the same treasury first, and C's
0.3 doesn't yet bring in enough to cover both. Protocol unchanged.
larder_test _test_livings.

## 525, terrain's side: the ground drawn from the relief

525 gave the ground a height in metres a cell (terrain "relief",
Relief.corner_heights, Relief.cliff_between); this draws it. Client only
(client3d.gd, border.gd); the castle and every level with no relief.png
draw exactly as before (their field is their whole levels, derived).

- One path, metres everywhere: Client3D._elevation(cell) (Relief.at, else
  the whole level) and _corner_heights(cell), the corners as drawn, kept per
  ground cell in _corners by _build_ground: Relief.corner_heights (each the
  mean of the cells joined to it walkably, per side of a cliff), a stair's
  ramp's (_ramp_heights: its high side up to the cell it climbs to) or a
  stream bed's under a bridge (_bed_levels, now metres). _height(cell)
  stays for whole-level logic only.
- The mesh: a vertex per corner and height (to the millimetre), so walkable
  neighbours share theirs and each side of a cliff has its own; normals the
  faces' about each vertex (the field's gradient there). No subdivision:
  one vertex a corner reads smooth at the game's camera on the sample's
  rise; 2x2 a cell stays the remedy if a remade hill shows facets.
- A point's height (_height_in) is the triangle the mesh draws there, not
  bilinear, so puppets, scatter, trees, rocks and props stand on what is
  drawn; _tile_position (a cell's middle) too. Marks (hover, ripple) tilt
  with the ground by its corners, not only on a stair.
- Cliffs: a face wherever two neighbours' corners part (Relief's rule
  decides where they part); a pond's shore stands over its water (525's
  lip), so its lip is a low face down to the bed. Water, where the level
  gives its relief: the surface follows its cells, each corner the mean of
  the water cells' surfaces round it (_water_corner), so a pond is flat and
  a stream slopes down its valley (flat steps each a body overlapped as a
  staircase of see-through sheets); the bed under it (water and fords,
  _wet) each corner the lower of its own and the surface's, sunk
  WATER_BED_DEPTH (a ford FORD_DEPTH 0.06), a bank's face going down to it.
  A level with no relief.png keeps its water as before.
- Buildings, bridges, wall bases, posts and towers stand at their cells'
  elevation (pads are flat by 525's parse); the forest's border and grown
  trees take the ground in metres (_elevations, rise 1.0; border.gd reads
  it as a float).
- Picking: the cursor's ray walked down from where it comes level with the
  highest ground (PICK_STEP 0.2 m across), then halved in to the ground as
  drawn, slopes included.
- The camera: its target follows the player's puppet, on the ground. Where
  the ground between it and the player stands over the line to them (a
  ridge: RIDGE_REACH 14 m back along the camera's way, kept RIDGE_CLEAR 0.3
  under the line to RIDGE_AIM 1 m over their feet), its pitch rises to
  clear it (ridge_pitch, eased at RIDGE_EASE 40 degrees a second), and
  settles back. None on a level with no relief.

tests/view_test (the sample: corners as the sim's, a thing on a slope on
the drawn triangle, each body of water level, the camera over a ridge and
not on the flat; on hills a stream's surface sloping down its valley, each
corner its water's mean, its bed under it; the castle drawn as its whole
levels; the stair, ledge and
rock checks in metres, no face where the sim walks but a shore's lip; on
levels/hills a face down each of its cliff steps, the plateau's west face,
and none on the thousands of steps down its slopes).

Rejected: bilinear heights (a puppet would float or sink up to a few
centimetres off the drawn triangles); a vertex a cell's middle (twice the
vertices for no gain at this camera); fading the ground that hides the
player (ground is not a wall; lifting the camera shows the slope).

## 530. A test scene that dies at launch is retried once, and the suite starts its scenes apart

Two landings on 2026-10-19 failed on a scene that never ran: builder's
companion_test exited 1 at 3 s after Godot's banner, and maps' items_test
exited 127 at 1 s with an empty log. Both passed alone and on the retry.
Both died in a suite's first burst, about nine Godots (six scenes, net_test,
state_test, the server export) started in the same instant, with memory to
spare (the gate saw 7.6 and 10.0 GB of commit used, about 30 GB free). Nothing
in the game or the runner exits 127, and a failed exec under timeout would
have written its error into the log: Windows failing to start the process,
handed back as a bare code, fits.

- The suite (tests/run.sh, run.ps1) starts its scenes 0.2 s apart, and
  land.sh / land.ps1 its parts 0.3 s apart.
- A launch failure: a scene exiting non-zero within 5 s whose output holds
  nothing after Godot's banner (no line of the game's own, no RESULT). One
  that ran any of its own code is never retried.
- One is noted (`heavy_job.py note <tree> launch <detail>`: the gate's log,
  with the exit code, where timeout and Godot resolve, and the machine's free
  RAM and commit; `heavy_job summary` lists and counts them) and run once
  more after 2 s. A retry that dies at launch too fails the scene, both
  diagnoses in its verdict.
- The scene's verdict line says "retried after a launch failure: ...", and the
  SUITE line counts them, passed or not, so the rate stays visible.
- net_test, state_test and the server boot are not retried (they run outside
  the suite's runner).

tests/heavy_job_test (note takes only its events, logs free memory, the
summary counts it); run.sh and run.ps1 checked against a fake Godot (127
once then a pass: retried, passes; banner-only twice: fails with both
notes; a "[net]" line then exit 1: not retried).

Rejected: retrying any failed scene (it would hide flaky tests); fewer
scenes at once (slower landings for a failure that is rare).

Amended (release's go, 2026-10-20): perf's 543 landing lost anim_rig_test
to a segfault at launch (exit 139 at 5 s: the banner, then the engine's
crash-handler block, no line of the game's; it passes alone 3 of 3). That
block now counts as nothing of the scene's own (run.sh's LAUNCH_ONLY, run.ps1's
$launchOnly: the banner, blank lines, the "====" rules, CrashHandlerException,
Engine version, Dumping the backtrace, Load address, the "[n]" frames, "-- END
OF ... BACKTRACE --"), so it gets the one retry. A crash that is
deterministic on load still fails twice, and one after any line of the game's
own, or after RESULT, is never retried.
- The launch note carries the crash, its top frame and the whole backtrace
  (frame symbols, "main+40d4d61 ...") to the gate's log; the verdict line shows
  it up to the top frame. heavy_job summary groups launch crashes by top
  frame ("launch crashes by top frame: main+40d4d61 2"): the same frame again
  and again is an engine or asset bug to chase.
- The window is 10 s, was 5: the segfault's own dump took 5 s, and under the
  day's load a fake Godot exiting 127 at once was read at 6 s, missing its
  retry in 2 of 4 runs at 5 s, none of 3 at 10 s. The content is the guard.
Checked against fake Godots in both runners (a crash block once then a pass:
retried, passes; a game line then the crash: not retried); heavy_job_test
(two crashes with one top frame grouped, the backtrace kept out of the
summary).

Amended (2) (release, 2026-10-20; ui's net_test at 22:04 lost an instance to
a segfault, which only bash's "Segmentation fault" line showed): net_test.sh's
quit() keeps each instance's exit code, and one that died on a signal (128 or
more) is noted in the gate's log as a launch event, its role (server, server2,
client4, ...) and, from its log, the crash, top frame and whole backtrace in
run.sh's form, so heavy_job summary groups net_test's crashes by top frame
with the suite's. Observability only: nothing in net_test is retried. Checked
with a process killed by SIGSEGV over a crash block (noted, grouped) beside a
clean exit (not noted).

## 536. Talk with no panel: offers spoken and taken by a word

Jeff, from play (2026-10-19): "the questions at the bottom don't seem natural
when every npc is the same... I'd rather not have the ui at all". ui's side
takes the conversation panel away (E or a click addresses the say line, a
HUD hint while an offer stands); this is npc's: an offer is heard, and
taken, in words. A line said to a resident (336) that asks for wares, work
or news, by word lists in levels/residents.json offers "asks" (Jeff's to
tune; the defaults in Offers.ASKS), is answered without the mind:
Offers.to_speak picks the first fresh offer of the kinds that ask names
(wares: the shop line; work: a commission, a plea, the building fund, the
scholar's page; news: the rumour, the page) and Main speaks its "words" as
the body's speech and the party log's line, exactly as written, noted
"[offer]" in the transcript and "offer" in mind.log; asked again, the next
of that kind, round and round; nothing is volunteered. What was spoken
stands for that player (Main._standing, one per player, memory only) until
taken, refused, replaced by another ask, a day old, or the body out of
hearing. A yes word, an amount said ("give 25", "lend 5", a bare number),
or the name of the thing or person (Offers.named: the shop item, the
captive or kin, "the rest" / "what I have" for the fund's second line,
"debt", "page") takes the offer named, else the one standing, through the
same Offers.accept and Main._accept_offer as the panel did; a yes to a debt
pays what is owed or all they have, a yes to the fund its step, "the rest"
the whole lack; the GIVE accept now takes a said amount; over the purse or
the cap it is refused in words ("You have but 9 gold.", "The inn wants but
24 gold more.", "I owe but 14."), nothing taken. A no clears what stands
with nothing said back. Any other line is the mind's, as before, and the
mind still carries the offers as facts. The "offers" message gains
"standing": {id, title} when one stands (absent otherwise), for ui's hint:
PROTOCOL_REVISION 23 (release: an added key in an existing message bumps,
as 17 and 21 did). The "offer" command verb and the message's list stay, so
a client may still accept by id. offers_test (the rules, pure) and

## 533, economy's side: yields kept a day as the seasons lengthen

Environment's 533 (Jeff's tone package) makes a season 14 days, not 7. A
crop's growth is per season, a harvest, the winter's roots and a
shearing once a season, so at 14 days a day's food and wool would halve.
Rather than doubling economy.json's numbers in step with the box's
console, Towns.season_scale() (Season.season_days over the 7 the rules
are set for, SEASON_DAYS_RULED) scales crop.harvest, crop.roots and
flock.wool: 1 at 7 days, 2 at 14, the same a day either way, landed
before 533 so the box never runs the longer seasons without it.
farm_test _test_season_scale. Protocol unchanged.

## 539. A landing checks the CHANGELOG before its tests

On 2026-10-19 four bullets went in the wrong place. Economy's 522 and maps'
amended 525 went into released sections (v0.1.157's, v0.1.158's), and
terrain's forge and 528 bullets were left under Unreleased beside their
released copies. A rebase keeps a bullet beside the heading it was next to,
and a release cut moves that heading. Each slip ships wrong release notes or
none.

- tools/changelog_check.py, run first by tests/land.sh and land.ps1: no
  Godot, before any wait at the gate. A failure names the bullet and what to
  do ("move it under ## Unreleased"; "drop it: vX.Y.Z already carries it";
  "make it as tagged"), and the landing fails.

  tag vX.Y.Z's CHANGELOG.md, blank lines included (line ends as the
  repository keeps them). At a cut the newest heading is not tagged yet
  (the suite runs before release_client tags it): then the section below is
  checked against its own tag.
- No bullet line under ## Unreleased may also stand in a released section.
- Tags are fetched first (git fetch -q --tags). A tag that cannot be had is
  a warning, not a failure.

## 537. Building codes and cell coordinates in builder mode

Jeff (via the coordinator): "in build mode it could mark coordinates and
name buildings with a code?" Small, client-side, as the coordinator
approved.

- A building's code is its kind's or slot's first letter, upper case,
  and a number: H3 (a house or hut), S1 (a shed), B2 (a bridge).
  Level.building_codes derives them in level.json order: an entry's own
  "code", else the next number past the highest that letter has had.
  Level.fill_codes writes them into the entries, and keeps level.json's
  "building_codes" (letter -> the last number given) at each letter's
  highest. MapDoc.save and builder mode (each tool, and a session's
  level) call it.
- Stable under edits: adding a building gives it the next number;
  removing one leaves every other code as it was, and its code is never
  given again once written (the counter keeps it). A copy repeating a
  code (a paste) gets its own. A stamped prefab's buildings drop the
  prefab's codes and are given the level's next ones.
- Level.parse gives each building its "code", so the client and the
  server work them out from the same level.json. Nothing new travels:
  protocol unchanged.
- On the client, while B is on: the HUD shows the cell under the cursor
  and the player's own ("212, 207      you 210, 205"); each building
  carries its code and name floating over it (Client3D.show_building_codes,
  kept over a rebuilt level); a click on one says in the party log "H3
  house at 212, 207, facing south, use: inn". At any time the cursor hint
  over a building is its code and name (after the things' hints).
- Builder requests: the request lists the level's buildings by code, the
  grid's settings show each entry's "code", and set_building takes a code
  in place of a cell, so "make H3 the inn" works. Other tools still take
  cells, read from the listing.
- The admin console's move takes a code: "move <player> H3 [zone]" lands
  at the cell outside the middle of its front (main.front_of), the
  nearest walkable as before.

builder_test _test_codes; editor_test's every-key list (building_codes
not offered).
## 528 amended: the officials paid first, at a living

The coordinator, after 528's soak (officials unpaid 229, the floor and
the makers' price drawing on the treasury first); Jeff: "the town pays
official jobs", "wages are paid by town". The coordinator flags the wage
to Jeff as his to move.
- An official's wage the treasury can't pay is owed (Production
  _official_wages: worker "owed", never past store.owed_cap), not lost,
  and each tick what the town owes its officials is paid before anyone
  else's debts (Economy._pay_head_first, then the head build's
  suppliers, then the rest in turn). Economy.is_official.
- The officials' wage is 4 a day (official.<trade>.every 54000), not 4
  every 18000 (12 a day).
Three soaks (30 days, 3 players, on the same main) give the reasoning:
1. A day of the officials' wages and what is owed them held back above
   the floor ahead of everything (deliveries, the floor, other debts):
   the town froze. Nothing was built after day 2.4, no inn, the wage
   floor paid 0 of 280, the farmer's deliveries owed.
2. Owed officials paid first among debts, nothing held back, at 12 a
   day: still starved. The farmer's income 2.6 a day (13.4), no inn, the
   floor paid 39 of 319. The officials' 36 a day between three was more
   than the treasury takes in and four times an official's keep (2.5 to
   4 a day): "goes unpaid" had been hiding a wrong number, not a
   shortfall.
3. As 2 at 4 a day: the officials were due 324 and paid all of it (76
   on the day, 248 owed and paid later); the inn on day 16.2, treasury
   end 5, the floor 252 due, 133 paid, 119 owed.
The standing fact: with today's inflows (rent, taxes, caravans, the
luxury tax and C's tax on the rich's services) the treasury can't pay
the wage floor, the officials and the makers' price all at once; the
floor runs about half owed. The next gold has to come from trade's
volume or from the rich, not from the poor. larder_test, return_test.
Protocol unchanged.
